title: Refusal healing re-evaluates on a possibly stale binding, so a grant_scope_mismatch after a long park fails once by construction with stale_fence
outcome: When Begin-refusal healing re-evaluates and the binding it reuses has been re-fenced (for example, after a long park), the host rebinds once and re-evaluates within the same remaining budget, or refreshes the binding before reuse. The head is then delivered without a Resume, and a definite refusal still ends in a durable, actionable hold.
acceptance: Fail-first: a production-path test with a scripted transport and clock and no synthetic load. A Begin is refused grant_scope_mismatch after the session's binding was re-fenced; on unchanged code the healing re-evaluate is refused stale_fence, the head is terminal, and a Resume is needed. After the fix, the same sequence delivers the head exactly once without Resume: after the healing re-evaluate is refused stale_fence, the host rebinds once and re-evaluates once more, within the remaining admission budget.

A second stale_fence after the fresh rebind, or an exhausted budget, ends in a durable, actionable hold naming the code. There is never more than one healing rebind per admission, and no retry loop. Tests cover both.
The existing stale_fence-first path (engram_host_adapter.rs:5320) and the other healable codes keep their behaviour; existing tests stay green.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
